digest.component_or_area: outbound parent write surfaces and adapters
propositions: A CREATE emit that drops a non-epic parent (slot 2) logs debug-level only; no durable bridge_alerts entry is created, violating the project's contract that undelivered parent changes must leave an operator-visible record.

An ACLI attach fallback that receives HTTP 400 on set_parent (slot 4) warns and returns silently without calling record_parent_divergence; the parent rejection is invisible to operators despite the track write having already succeeded.
The two silent-drop surfaces are outside the file_impact of ticket 9f26, which fixed the same issue on UPDATE emit (slot 1), requiring separate fix and test coverage.

The non-epic parent guard is unconditional in code but documented only as a Cloud/next-gen constraint; Data Center accepts and ignores such parents rather than rejecting them, creating a doc/code divergence.

The fix must distinguish bound from unbound parents: unbound parents must stay silent because they converge on a later pass, whereas bound parents that are dropped represent a real hierarchy loss requiring alert.
